title: Brain Connectivity Map with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create an interactive 3D brain connectivity map visualization using Three.js with a physics debug overlay. Load the 'horse.glb' model using GLTFLoader as a decorative anatomical reference model positioned to the right side of the scene.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark background (0x0a0a1a)
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 15), looking at origin
- AmbientLight (0x334466, intensity 0.5) and DirectionalLight (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (5,10,5)
- OrbitControls for camera rotation

BRAIN NETWORK:
- Create 12 sphere nodes (radius 0.3) representing brain regions arranged in a roughly ellipsoidal shape centered at origin. Use positions like: (-3,2,0), (-2,3,1), (-1,2,2), (0,3,0), (1,2,2), (2,3,1), (3,2,0), (-2,0,-1), (0,1,-2), (2,0,-1), (-1,-1,0), (1,-1,0)
- Each node should have an emissive material with colors varying by region (use a gradient from blue 0x0066ff to red 0xff3300 based on index)
- Label each node with a CSS2DRenderer label or sprite text: 'Frontal-L', 'Parietal-L', 'Temporal-L', 'Cingulate', 'Temporal-R', 'Parietal-R', 'Frontal-R', 'Occipital-L', 'Cerebellum', 'Occipital-R', 'Thalamus-L', 'Thalamus-R'
- Draw connection lines between nodes using THREE.Line with varying opacity/thickness to represent connectivity strength. Create at least 20 connections with random strengths between 0.1 and 1.0. Store connections as an array of {from, to, strength}.

HORSE MODEL:
- Load horse.glb using GLTFLoader
- Scale it to 0.02 and position at (8, -2, 0)
- Apply a wireframe material override (0x44ff88) to make it look like a debug/reference model
- Add a label 'Anatomical Reference' above it

PHYSICS DEBUG OVERLAY:
- Each node has a simple physics simulation: nodes gently oscillate (sine wave, amplitude 0.1-0.3, varying frequencies 0.5-2.0 Hz) to simulate neural activity pulses
- When a node is 'active', it pulses (scales up to 1.5x then back) over 0.5 seconds
- Connection lines should pulse with a traveling glow effect along their length
- Implement a debug overlay toggle: when enabled, show velocity vectors as small arrows on each node, and bounding spheres (wireframe) around each node

UI ELEMENTS:
- A button with id 'toggleDebug' labeled 'Toggle Debug Overlay' in top-left corner
- A button with id 'activateRandom' labeled 'Activate Random Node' that triggers a random node activation pulse
- A button with id 'toggleConnections' labeled 'Toggle Connections' to show/hide connection lines
- A dropdown select with id 'viewMode' with options: 'normal', 'heatmap', 'wireframe'. In heatmap mode, node colors map to activity level (red=high, blue=low). In wireframe mode, all nodes become wireframe.
- A div with id 'infoPanel' showing: currently selected node name, its connections count, and current activity level
- A slider with id 'activitySpeed' (range 0.1 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) controlling oscillation speed multiplier

INTERACTION:
- Click on a node (raycasting) to select it. Selected node gets a highlight ring (torus) around it. Update infoPanel.
- Press 'D' key to toggle debug overlay (same as button)
- Press 'Space' to activate all nodes simultaneously (cascade activation)
- Press 'R' to reset all nodes to default state

STATE MANAGEMENT - Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- nodeCount: number of brain nodes (should be 12)
- connectionCount: number of connections
- debugOverlayVisible: boolean
- connectionsVisible: boolean
- selectedNodeIndex: index of selected node (-1 if none)
- selectedNodeName: string name of selected node ('' if none)
- viewMode: 'normal'|'heatmap'|'wireframe'
- activitySpeedMultiplier: current speed multiplier
- activeNodeCount: number of currently pulsing/active nodes
- horseLoaded: boolean (true when horse.glb loaded)
- allNodesActivated: boolean (true during cascade)
- frameCount: incrementing frame counter
- nodesPositions: array of {x,y,z} current positions for all nodes
- physicsValid: boolean, true if no NaN in any node position
physics_constraints: Nodes oscillate with sinusoidal motion. No node position should ever contain NaN. Nodes must stay within a bounding box of (-5,-3,-4) to (5,5,4). Activity pulses propagate along connections with a delay proportional to connection length. Speed multiplier affects all oscillation frequencies uniformly.
